summary: Joint partner workshop focused on surfacing priority accounts for co-sell pilots, aligning on deal protection and margining, and scoping technical benchmarks to accelerate close. Outcome: agreed artifacts to exchange (one-pager, account list, benchmark matrix) and scheduling of a SE technical pre-sprint.
topics: co-sell motion, account prioritization, deal protection, margining, technical benchmark scoping, security/VPC constraints, close plan
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. we'll do a quick round then jump into the velocity hack details.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi! Priya here, thanks Maya, excited — we've been wanting to tighten the joint motion. Carlos and Eun-ji on.
[00:18] Carlos Menendez: Hey all. quick note, got back-to-back but staying for the agenda.
[00:23] Dmitri Ivanov: Dmitri from Redwood SE team, I'll take point on the benchmark scoping.
[00:27] Noah Patel: Noah, CSM, here to keep the pilot timelines honest.
[00:31] Maya Chen: cool. high-level — goal for today's hackathon: pick 2-3 pilot accounts to co-sell in the next 6–8 weeks, agree on revenue split guardrails, and scope the technical validation (latency, token cost, security).
[00:44] Priya Rao: sounds good. internal ask from Tessara leadership is we need clear deal protection — we can't introduce conflict with our existing reseller partners.
[00:52] Maya Chen: understood. typical patterns — lead-assigned, carveouts, and minimum-term protections. we can draft language; legal will need to review but we can put guardrails in the one-pager.
[01:05] Eun-ji Park: on the tech side, most of our customers require VPC peering or private link. can Redwood support a private deployment or dedicated capacity for pilots?
[01:15] Dmitri Ivanov: yes — Redwood Dedicated is exactly for that. dedicated pools and VPC options. interoperability note: there are some latency tradeoffs for on-prem vs hosted, we'll quantify.
[01:26] Carlos Menendez: cost matters — if the model path bumps up deal economics we need margin to Tessara's channel. how do we propose splits?
[01:34] Maya Chen: we typically propose three options: hosted referral (low revenue share), co-sell with shared margin (mid), and joint P&L on Dedicated for large accounts (higher share to partner). we'll lay out ranges in the one-pager.
[01:45] [01:45] Priya Rao: okay. can we get an example math for a mid-sized SaaS deal? like ARR 400k, expected LLM infra 8k/mo — how much to Tessara?
[01:55] Maya Chen: yes — we'll mock two scenarios. but quick answer: referral might be 10–15%, co-sell 20–35% depending on contribution, and dedicated carve could be structure-based. we'll pull a table.
[02:08] Dmitri Ivanov: technical caveat — model choice will alter token costs. if we select a 70B dense vs a quantized 13B variant cost delta can be 2–3x. we should align on models for each pilot so economics are consistent.
[02:22] Eun-ji Park: good point. also, our customers in EU insist on data residency — we need region mapping and whether Redwood can pin region or deploy private.
[02:32] Maya Chen: Redwood Private can handle VPC+region pins. we'll note region availability in the one-pager; for immediate pilots we can use hosted EU instances if data flow controls are acceptable.
[02:45] [02:45] Carlos Menendez: competitively, a few incumbents (Anthropic/OpenAI) are pitching low-cost inference w/ big brand recognition. what's Redwood's edge here?
[02:55] Maya Chen: production economics and control — predictable latency, smart routing, caching to reduce token spend, and a clear path to dedicated/private which incumbents sometimes bolt on slowly. plus we have observability hooks to show cost per token per route — that resonates with finance teams.
[03:12] Priya Rao: on the GTM side, Tessara can bring warm leads with champions. we want co-sell content: joint deck, case study template, and a playbook for discovery qualification.
[03:23] Noah Patel: we'll share a starter co-sell deck and a qualification checklist. also will add a templated close plan: champion, exec sponsor, PoC success criteria, procurement path.
[03:35] Maya Chen: perfect. shifting to account prioritization — Priya, you mentioned a short list of eight? can you surface the headcount and champion for each?
[03:46] Priya Rao: yes, I'm putting that together. some are in early eval, two are already trialing LLM infra. I'll annotate risk.
[03:53] [03:53] Dmitri Ivanov: for the two pilot candidates we should define benchmark metric matrix: cold start latency p50/p95, steady-state throughput, per-token cost under typical seq lengths, model quality on a small eval set (F1/accuracy per use case). I'll send a template.
[04:13] Eun-ji Park: also include end-to-end latency from Tessara's app to Redwood inference and back — network hops matter.
[04:20] Maya Chen: agreed. next: timing. we propose a 2-week technical sprint (SE-led) to run benchmarks and a parallel sales push with Tessara reps. aim to have a signed pilot agreement within 6 weeks. realistic?
[04:34] Carlos Menendez: yes if we get exec-sponsor buy-in. procurement often takes 3 weeks, legal another 2 for MSAs. so 6 is tight but doable.
[04:44] Priya Rao: can Redwood provide a pilot-friendly MSA template or a low-friction SOW? our procurement teams like simple playbooks.
[04:52] Maya Chen: we'll attach a pilot SOW template in the one-pager bundle.
[05:00] [05:00] Carlos Menendez: what about partner registration / deal protection mechanics? Tessara needs a logging mechanism so our rep gets credit if Tessara introduced lead.
[05:09] Maya Chen: we have CRM tagging recommendations and can support co-sell registration in our partner portal. action item: Priya to list champions and dates; Maya to propose registration rules.
[05:20] Dmitri Ivanov: quick technical question from Eun-ji — for KV cache and continuous batching, do you have any constraints on sequence lengths? we have customers with 4k seq and some with 16k.
[05:33] Maya Chen: Redwood runtime supports variable seq lengths; for very long sequences we recommend specific model variants and tuning to avoid throughput cliffs. we'll call that out in the benchmark matrix.
[05:45] Eun-ji Park: great. for security/compliance — do you have SOC 2 and ISO docs? also KMS integration?
[05:53] Noah Patel: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in flight and we support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated. we'll put links to the compliance pack in the shared drive.
[06:08] Priya Rao: can we get a short security bullet list for partner-facing execs — so when Tessara engages a CIO we have one-pager?
[06:16] Maya Chen: yes we'll add a security one-liner page: SOC2/ISO, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS/HSM support, RBAC, audit logs.
[06:26] [06:26] Carlos Menendez: on enablement — Tessara reps need a 60–90 minute live demo and a cheat sheet for qualifying LLM use cases.
[06:35] Maya Chen: we'll host a 60m enablement session + record and leave a one-pager cheat sheet.
[06:41] Priya Rao: and co-marketing? Tessara wants joint logos on a pilot announcement if we get first revenue.
[06:47] Maya Chen: yes we can do a co-marketing clause in the one-pager — marketing approvals required.
[06:52] [06:52] Dmitri Ivanov: circling back to benchmarks — Dmitri will run initial tests using our 13B quantized variant and also a 70B dense to show tradeoffs. will include tokenization breakouts and per-request cost.
[07:05] Eun-ji Park: can you share the test harness link? we prefer reproducible scripts.
[07:10] Dmitri Ivanov: will send link to GitHub repo and a spreadsheet for result capture.
[07:15] Maya Chen: okay let's recap decisions and owners. agreed pilots: two accounts (Priya to share list), deliverables: one-pager + SOW + benchmark matrix + enablement session. timeline: SE pre-sprint next week, pilot SOW within 2–3 weeks, goal to sign pilots within 6 weeks.
[07:35] Priya Rao: agreed. one ask — include a simple escalation path in the close plan (who to call at Redwood if we hit procurement stalls).
[07:43] Noah Patel: I'll add an escalation ladder with names and emails.
[07:47] Maya Chen: perfect. final open item: pricing elasticity — we'll show 2 price points for a trial — baseline and accelerated SLA.
[07:55] Carlos Menendez: thanks everyone — excited to move fast.
[08:00] Maya Chen: thanks all. Dmitri will follow up with benchmark templates; I'll share the co-sell one-pager. Priya we'll schedule the SE pre-sprint.
[08:08] [08:08] Action items and links: GitHub test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/partner-benchmarks (Dmitri to confirm access), Drive folder (one-pager + SOW + security pack): https://redwood.app/drive/partner/tessara-hackathon (placeholder).
[08:20] End of recording.
notes: Participants emphasized deal protection and simple legal artifacts; agreed pilot cadence and artifacts. There were some transcription errors on product names in a few places; SE to follow up with concrete benchmarks.
